human_tolerance.notes: Lives in urban and rural habitats; garden ponds are used for spawning. Large numbers are killed on roads by motor vehicles, and urban populations show lower genetic diversity.

phases.name: dormancy
phases.note: Typically hibernates from late October to January in the British Isles; hibernates in running water, muddy burrows or leaf litter and mud at the bottom of ponds.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: Spawning runs from late February to late June, generally peaking in April over most of the range. Range-wide window; no per-country dates were sourced.

vocalizations.description: Males give a short mating call at breeding ponds in spring; it differs from the call of the moor frog, which often breeds alongside it.

taxonomy.note: GBIF species 2426805 matches Rana temporaria Linnaeus, 1758 at species rank, status ACCEPTED, family Ranidae, class Amphibia. ITIS TSN 173444 is valid at species rank.

external.note: iNaturalist taxon 25591 (Rana temporaria, active, species rank) confirmed at the iNaturalist API. NCBI 8407, AmphibiaWeb 5168 and iNaturalist 25591 via Wikidata (P685, P5036, P3151).

common_names.note: Wikidata Q27465 labels: en common frog, fr grenouille rousse, de Grasfrosch, nl bruine kikker.

range.note: Country list derived from Wikipedia's 'found throughout much of Europe as far north as Scandinavia and as far east as the Urals, except for most of the Iberian Peninsula, southern Italy, and the southern Balkans'. Ireland is excluded: Wikipedia reports genetic evidence for native SW Irish populations but also long-standing introduction, so the status is unresolved. Iberia, the southern Balkans and Greece are excluded. Asia is not enumerated. Introduced: Faroe Islands (Wikipedia). Introductions to Lewis, Shetland and Orkney are inside GB and cannot be expressed at country level.

traits.body_plan.note: Vertebrate; a four-limbed frog (AmphiBIO and Wikipedia both describe an anuran body plan).

traits.limb_count.note: Four legs; Wikipedia describes long hind legs for swimming and hopping.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Hop and Swim: Wikipedia 'long hind legs adapted for swimming and hopping on land'; AmphiBIO Aqu 1. Walk is added because the shared anuran program uses the walk gait when foraging and wandering; no source describes walking for this species.

traits.thermoregulation.note: Wikipedia: 'As an ectotherm, the common frog is highly dependent on temperature'.

traits.skin.note: Wikipedia: moist skin, distinguishing it from the warty skin of the common toad.

traits.respiration.note: Lungs as the enum value. Wikipedia also describes oxygen uptake through the skin during hibernation, which the enum does not express.

traits.metamorphosis.note: Wikipedia: metamorphosis through an aquatic larva, a terrestrial juvenile and an adult.

traits.nest_type.note: Eggs are laid as clumps in shallow pond water; there is no constructed nest.

traits.size_class.note: From mass_kg (0.0227 kg, below the 0.05 kg Tiny threshold).

traits.mass_kg.note: Wikipedia: 'The average mass is 22.7 g (0.80 oz)'. AmphiBIO v1 Body_mass_g is 47.6 g for this taxon, roughly double; the Wikipedia value is used because it is the stated average adult mass. The disagreement is unresolved.

traits.length_m.note: Midpoint of Wikipedia 'a body length of 6 to 9 centimetres' (0.075 m). AmphiBIO Size_at_maturity_min/max_mm 50 to 83 (midpoint 66.5 mm) is a second, narrower reading; AmphiBIO Body_size_mm 110 is not used as an adult typical length.

traits.lifespan_y.note: Midpoint of Wikipedia 'common frogs will typically live between six and eight years'. AmphiBIO Longevity_max_y 27 is a maximum and is not used.

traits.diet.note: Wikipedia lists invertebrate prey only (crane flies, moth and butterfly larvae, woodlice, arachnids, beetles, slugs, snails, earthworms). AmphiBIO Arthro 1 and Vert NA agree. The 1.0 share is an authored allocation; no vertebrate prey is reported.

traits.social.note: Wikipedia: 'Outside the breeding season, common frogs live a solitary life'. Group sizes of 1 are an authored reading.

traits.activity_pattern.note: AmphiBIO flags Diu 1 and Noc 1 with Crepu NA, so the cathemeral value follows the dataset. Wikipedia says frogs hide in damp places during the day and begin searching for food at night. The shared program models nocturnal foraging; see the Cathemeral and behaviour limitation in the PR.

traits.defense.note: Flee is an authored choice. Wikipedia names predators and says the frog hides in water, but does not state an escape response.

habitat.use.note: Authored shares. AmphiBIO flags Ter 1, Aqu 1 and Arb 1 without shares. Wikipedia describes damp wetland niches near ponds and hibernation in ponds, burrows and leaf litter.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Wikipedia: frogs hide in damp places and live 'among long riparian grass' and in 'layers of decaying leaves and mud'.

habitat.resources.note: Prey, spawning ponds in February to June (Wikipedia) and winter burrows and leaf litter (Wikipedia). Weights and the burrow months are authored where the source names no value.

habitat.suitability.note: Authored distance-to-water curve: full suitability at a pond, 0.3 at 500 m, zero by 2000 m. Wikipedia gives no distance threshold.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Wikipedia: frogs make homes 'in both urban and rural environments'; garden ponds used for spawning; 'large numbers are killed on the roads by motor vehicles'. Urban populations show lower genetic diversity and higher mortality.

seasonal.strategy.note: Wikipedia: 'normally active for much of the year, only hibernating in the coldest months'.

seasonal.triggers.note: Authored temperatures and day counts. No open source gives thresholds for this species.

seasonal.phases.note: Dormancy for GB from Wikipedia's 'In the British Isles, common frogs typically hibernate from late October to January'. Breeding from Wikipedia's 'late February and late June'. No FR-specific dormancy dates were sourced, so France follows the trigger rule only.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Egg duration: 17.5 days, the midpoint of 'usually takes 2–3 weeks for the eggs to hatch'. Juvenile: 1095 days from 'Sexual maturity occurs only after three years'. Tadpole has no sourced duration and is left out.

vocalizations.croak.note: Wikipedia: males 'emit a mating call' at the birth pond, and the two species have different calls. Months follow the breeding window. Cooldown is authored; no source gives call timing or frequency.

look.note: Wikipedia: olive green to grey-brown back, with dark blotches, a chevron on the neck and a dark spot behind the eye; white or yellow underside. Palette and proportions are authored.

behavior.note: Authored parameters for the shared nocturnal anuran program: the call id and the March–April call months, which are the only two months the program can enable.
